title: Quantum Physics III
description: Perturbation theory, time-dependent processes, scattering and identical particles.
cosmologyNeeds: Reaction rates and scattering cross sections decide when particles fell out of equilibrium in the early universe: the basis of Big Bang nucleosynthesis and of dark-matter relic abundances.
notes: Lectures follow MIT's 24 video lectures (Spring 2018, Zwiebach), each split into short videos with their own transcripts; the syllabus links each lecture's first video. Zwiebach's lecture notes (CC BY-NC-SA) cover the same topics in eight chapters; Chapter 5 (Particles in electromagnetic fields) is marked not available on OCW, so Lectures 13–14 rely on their transcripts.

syllabus.title: Non-degenerate perturbation theory
Perturbation series; anharmonic oscillator; degenerate perturbation theory
Degenerate perturbation theory: good bases, degeneracy resolved to first and second order
Hydrogen fine structure: scales, coupled basis, Pauli and Dirac equations
Fine structure: Darwin, relativistic and spin-orbit corrections
Zeeman effect; the semiclassical approximation
The WKB approximation and connection formulae
Airy functions and the derivation of the connection formulae
Time-dependent perturbation theory: the interaction picture
Constant perturbations and Fermi's golden rule
Harmonic perturbations; stimulated emission and absorption; ionization of hydrogen
Ionization rate of hydrogen; two-level atoms and Einstein's argument
Thermal radiation, Einstein's A and B coefficients; charged particles in electromagnetic fields
Gauge invariance; magnetic field on a torus; Landau levels
Adiabatic invariants, classical and quantum
The quantum adiabatic theorem; Landau–Zener transitions
Berry's phase; molecules and energy scales
The Born–Oppenheimer approximation
Scattering: amplitude, cross sections and partial waves
Phase shifts and the optical theorem
Computing phase shifts; the integral equation for scattering
The Born approximation; identical particles
Permutation operators
Symmetrizer, antisymmetrizer and the symmetrization postulate
